contributions.original_prompts:
New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-orchestration-retries-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-orchestration-retries-2026.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-orchestration-retries.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration/retries`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration/retries, November describes private-preview cross-processor retries with distinct Main and Retry processor roles. An entitled user opens Dashboard Payments > Orchestration > Rules and sets the processors in an Action. To change an existing rule, duplicate it and edit the draft. The separate Rules guide explains that draft edits take effect only after activation in the relevant environment. November adds an email-request path for access to the preview. Requesting access does not grant it (old raw lines 10-22 and 36-40, new raw lines 11-24 and 38-54). If 3DS is attempted on the first main-processor attempt and authentication fails, or it succeeds but that payment still fails, Orchestration skips the alternate processor and sends payment_intent.payment_failed. A feature missing on the retry processor also makes it ineligible. A Stripe-main block such as a Radar block is treated as a decline for retry. Adaptive Acceptance enabled on Stripe can add a Stripe-side attempt before cross-processor retry when Stripe is main, or a possible additional attempt after the cross-processor retry when Stripe is retry processor (old raw lines 24-34, new raw lines 26-36). source-stripe-orchestration-retries.md captures the four branches but omits the draft and access boundaries and the Stripe-main block qualifier. Attempt or configuration is distinct from payment success.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/orchestration/retries, the only substantive addition to the guide is a documented email request and registration example for the existing private preview (old raw lines 36-40, new raw lines 38-54). The new anchor navigates to the request. Heading spacing and list numbering are presentational. Keep the May main/retry roles, duplicate-and-edit draft requirement, 3DS and compatibility exclusions, Stripe-main block example and optional Adaptive Acceptance order dated. None changes in November (old raw lines 10-34, new raw lines 11-36). In source-stripe-orchestration-retries.md and the reciprocal concept and feature-support routes, qualify 'no retry' for an incompatible feature as skipping the chosen processor. The May and November feature-support guides say opt-in error protection may route a payment requesting an unsupported feature to Stripe. In cross-processor failover following an original Stripe attempt, Stripe ignores the error-protection configuration to avoid a second attempt on Stripe. A compatible configured alternate can still receive an otherwise eligible cross-processor retry. The November routing guide says Stripe checks that alternate and skips it if it lacks the required feature (raw/stripe-orchestration-feature-support-2026.md lines 12–16; raw/stripe-payments-orchestration-feature-support-2026-11-07.md lines 25–29; raw/stripe-payments-orchestration-route-payments-2026-11-07.md lines 222–226). Separate the documented HTTP 400 orchestration_unsupported request validation, whose message names the first unsupported feature, from the payment_intent.payment_failed webhook after first-attempt 3DS on the main processor when authentication fails or the payment fails after successful authentication (November retry raw line 30). A normal cross-processor retry uses the configured alternate. When Adaptive Acceptance is enabled, it can add a separate Stripe-side attempt before the cross-processor retry with Stripe as main, or after Stripe receives a cross-processor retry as the retry processor (November retry raw lines 28–36). These qualifications come from the companion guides and the unchanged retry cases. Rule edits, sandbox activation and preview-access requests supply no evidence of live activation. A fallback or Adaptive Acceptance attempt does not establish any successful payment or settlement.
